\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بہرحال} (baharhāl)}{بہرحال (baharhāl)}]{\ur{بہرحال} (baharhāl) — anyway; in any case}

\label{lesson:UR-C542-baharhal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a point (that things come to), then the Urdu for supposing (for argument's sake).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بہرحال}}
\textbf{\ur{بہرحال}} — \emph{baharhāl} — \textquotedblleft{}anyway; in any case\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بہرحال،} \ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{آئے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہمیں} \ur{خوشی} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baharhāl, agar āp āe to hameṅ khushī ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Anyway, if you come, we will be glad.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بہرحال}} (\emph{baharhāl}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{ba-har-ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}in every state\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{ba}, \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{}, \emph{har}, \textquotedblleft{}every\textquotedblright{}, and Arabic \emph{ḥāl}, \textquotedblleft{}a state\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baharhāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baharhāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baharhāl, agar āp āe to hameṅ khushī ho gī.} — Anyway, if you come, we will be glad.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a point (that things come to), then the Urdu for supposing (for argument's sake), then say \emph{baharhāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بہرحال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Anyway; in any case\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خیر} (khair)}{خیر (khair)}]{\ur{خیر} (khair) — well (moving on)}

\label{lesson:UR-C542-khair}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for supposing (for argument's sake), then the Urdu for in any case.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خیر}}
\textbf{\ur{خیر}} — \emph{khair} — \textquotedblleft{}well (moving on)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{خیر،} \ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{چلیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khair, agar voh nahīṅ āyā to ham chaleṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Well, if he doesn't come, we'll leave.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خیر}} (\emph{khair}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khayr}, \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{}: all is well, let us move on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بالخصوص} (bilkhusūs)}{بالخصوص (bilkhusūs)}]{\ur{بالخصوص} (bilkhusūs) — especially; in particular}

\label{lesson:UR-C542-bilkhusus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for in any case, then the Urdu for well (moving on).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بالخصوص}}
\textbf{\ur{بالخصوص}} — \emph{bilkhusūs} — \textquotedblleft{}especially; in particular\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نکتہ} (nuktā)}{نکتہ (nuktā)}]{\ur{نکتہ} (nuktā) — a point (in an argument)}

\label{lesson:UR-C542-nukta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for well (moving on), then the Urdu for in particular.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نکتہ}}
\textbf{\ur{نکتہ}} — \emph{nuktā} — \textquotedblleft{}a point (in an argument)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہی} \ur{نکتہ} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{بات} \ur{ختم} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yihī nuktā hai to bāt khatm huī.}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{نکتہ}} (\emph{nuktā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{nukta}, \textquotedblleft{}a dot; a subtle point\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خلاصہ} (khulāsā)}{خلاصہ (khulāsā)}]{\ur{خلاصہ} (khulāsā) — a summary; the gist}

\label{lesson:UR-C542-khulasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for in particular, then the Urdu for a point (in an argument).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خلاصہ}}
\textbf{\ur{خلاصہ}} — \emph{khulāsā} — \textquotedblleft{}a summary; the gist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{خلاصہ} \ur{یہ} \ur{کہ} \ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{آئیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khulāsā yih ki agar vaqt huā to ham āeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{خلاصہ}} (\emph{khulāsā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khulāṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}an extract, the essence\textquotedblright{}.
